items.title: TikTok Agrees to $400 Million Settlement in U.S. Child Privacy Lawsuit
items.one_liner: Enforcement action under COPPA imposing a $400M fine on TikTok for user privacy violations.
items.summary: TikTok agreed to pay $400 million to settle a US federal lawsuit over COPPA child privacy violations. TikTok will pay $300 million immediately and $100 million contingent upon vacating a prior Musical.ly consent decree. The agreement resolves allegations of unlawful data collection on users under 13 and mandates enhanced parental controls.
key_facts: Settlement: $400 million ($300 million immediate, $100 million conditional)
Regulation: Children's Online Privacy Protection Act (COPPA)
items.bottom_line: ByteDance will pay $400 million to resolve major U.S. federal child data privacy charges, forcing stricter platform controls.

claims.text: TikTok agreed to pay $400 million to settle a US federal lawsuit over COPPA child privacy violations.
claims.support_span: The U.S. Department of Justice (DoJ) announced on Friday that ByteDance-owned TikTok will pay $400 million to settle a 2024 lawsuit accusing the company of violating child privacy laws in the country.

claims.text: TikTok will pay $300 million immediately and $100 million contingent upon vacating a prior Musical.ly consent decree.
claims.support_span: As part of the settlement, the social media platform will pay $300 million immediately, and an additional $100 million "upon entry of an order vacating a prior consent decree entered against TikTok’s predecessor, Musical.ly," the DoJ said in a press release.

items.one_liner: Practical architectural and security advice on securing Windows IPC named pipes against privilege escalation.
items.summary: Developers frequently misuse Windows named pipes by assuming local interprocess communication is inherently trusted. High-privilege services using named pipes can expose unsafe APIs to lower-privilege local applications or malware. Security engineers must enforce restrictive access control lists, separate authentication from authorization, and strictly verify impersonation contexts.
items.bottom_line: Local interprocess communication via named pipes requires explicit access controls and input validation to prevent privilege escalation attacks.

claims.support_span: Named pipes are often treated as private because they are used for communication between applications on the same computer. That assumption is unsafe.
